module_title: Basics of Matter Properties: Elasticity, Surface Tension, and Viscosity
introduction: Matter (solids, liquids, and gases) exhibits unique hidden properties when subjected to forces. Solids can stretch and bounce back, liquids can act like stretched elastic membranes, and fluids can resist flowing.

core_concepts.title: Elasticity
core_concepts.description:
It is the property of a solid body by virtue of which it tends to regain its original size and shape after the applied force (deforming force) is removed. 
Example: A rubber band or a steel spring.

core_concepts.title: Surface Tension
core_concepts.description:
It is the property of a liquid at rest by virtue of which its free surface behaves like a 'stretched elastic membrane' and tries to occupy the 'minimum possible surface area'. 
Result: This is why raindrops are perfectly spherical (a sphere has the minimum surface area for a given volume).

core_concepts.title: Viscosity
core_concepts.description:
It is the internal 'fluid friction' of a liquid or gas. It is the property by which a fluid opposes the relative motion between its different layers. 
Example: Honey is highly viscous (flows slowly), while water has low viscosity (flows easily).

core_concepts.title: Stress and Strain
core_concepts.description:
1. Stress: The restoring force set up per unit area inside a body when deformed. ($Stress = Force / Area$). Unit: $N/m^2$. 
2. Strain: The ratio of the change in dimension to the original dimension. It has NO unit and NO dimensions.

important_entities.name: Steel vs. Rubber
important_entities.key_fact: Steel is MORE elastic than rubber
important_entities.significance: A classic exam question! In physics, elasticity means the 'ability to return to the original shape quickly and forcefully'. Steel opposes deformation much more strongly and snaps back faster than rubber, making it more elastic.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Question: 'Why can water striders (insects) walk on water?' Students often answer 'buoyancy'. FALSE. They walk on water because of 'Surface Tension', which creates a film strong enough to support their tiny weight.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Whenever you see the word 'Viscous', just read it as 'Thick'. High viscosity means high thickness and slow flow.

exam_strategy_tips: Direct Question in SSC: 'The spherical shape of a small drop of rain is due to?' Answer: Surface Tension.
